# Overview

Use two datasets to explore relationships, fit basic linear regression models, and explain the results. First, model teaching score using age. Then, model life expectancy using continent for countries observed in 2007. Each model uses just one explanatory variable.

This file contains all project tasks and questions. Review the grading rubric before beginning.

Complete every TODO. Write explanations in the Markdown response areas outside the code chunks. Support your answers with your own output, include units, and add brief code comments where they help explain your decisions. Use DataCamp Chapters 1–3 and the assigned ModernDive reading as references.

# Setup

Install any missing packages once in the RStudio Console: `tidyverse`, `moderndive`, `gapminder`, `broom`, `rmarkdown`, and `knitr`. Keep installation commands out of this report.

The setup below is provided so everyone starts with the same data. `evals_ch5` is created from `moderndive::evals`; it is not a separate packaged dataset. The Gapminder data are restricted to 2007 so each row represents one country in the same year.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(tidyverse)
library(moderndive)
library(gapminder)
library(broom)

evals_ch5 <- moderndive::evals |>
  select(ID, score, age)

gap_2007 <- gapminder::gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007)
```

- Write R code inside the supplied code chunks and explanations in the response areas below them. You may add chunks if needed.
- Use `lm()` to fit both models. Each uses one predictor; a categorical predictor can have more than two groups.
- Display your results explicitly. If you save a summary or plot in an object, also display that object so it appears in the knitted report.
- For R help, use `?lm`, `?predict.lm`, `?broom::augment.lm`, or `?moderndive::get_regression_table` in the Console. The `get_regression_table()` function comes from `moderndive` and `augment()` comes from `broom`.
